02 / SMALL PROGRAMS. REAL PROGRESS.

More doing.
Less back-and-forth.

Some tasks need a sequence, not another conversation. Code Mode lets one Python program read files, use their results, and return what matters.

Dependent tool calls in a single run

Syntax and types checked before execution

Workspace policies and approvals stay in place

Explore Code Mode
A PROGRAM, NOT A PILE OF PROMPTSPYTHON
explore_workspace.py illustrative example
# Find the pieces.
listing = await call_tool(
    "list_files", {"path": "src"}
)

# Connect them in one run.
results = []
for path in listing["output"]["files"][:3]:
    result = await call_tool(
        "read_file", {"path": path}
    )
    results.append(result["output"])

# Bring back what matters.
results
Isolated computation. Explicit tool access.Monty ↗

05 / GOOD QUESTIONS

A few things
before you start.

Can I try it without an API key?+

Yes. After installing dependencies, run uv run agent-tui --demo. The offline demo needs no credentials and makes no network requests.

What runs inside the sandbox?+

Code Mode programs run in Monty, with no direct host filesystem or network access. They reach the workspace through validated tool calls, which keep workspace policies, middleware, and approvals in place.

Can I bring my own tools?+

Connect MCP servers, add SKILL.md workflows, or use middleware hooks. Python factories also let you replace components such as providers, prompts, tools, and routing.

How do I stay in control?+

Inspect tool traces and approve actions in the terminal. Press Esc to stop a running program, or launch with --read-only to disable mutating tools.
